input: digits is a nonempty Array of decimal digits 0 through 9 with length n <= 4294967294. It represents a nonnegative integer most-significant digit first, with no leading zero except the single-digit representation [0]. String inputs, when present, are primitive strings, not boxed strings. Integer values are primitive safe-integer Number, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt. Arrays are dense ordinary Arrays, not sparse arrays, proxies, subclasses or accessor-backed collections. There is no concurrent mutation or monkey-patching of standard built-ins. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Allocation and runtime resource limits still require qualification; this declared domain is not a capacity or completion guarantee.
return: The identical caller-owned digits sequence, updated to represent the input integer plus one in most-significant-first form; its length is n or n+1.
mutation_aliasing: Carry propagation overwrites caller-owned digit elements; all-nine carry prepends one to that same sequence. Return identity is exactly the input sequence. No Solution instance state survives.
numeric: Only digits, indices and a single-digit increment are used. A changed digit stays in [0, 9]; there is no conversion of the whole represented value to Number or int. The n + 1 output-length bound fits a JavaScript Array.
complexity: O(n) worst-case time including in-place leading insertion; O(1) scalar auxiliary state, excluding runtime resizing storage for the caller-owned output sequence.
